paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the best gift God can give is Himself. The land was flowing with milk and honey, and the angel was ready to drive out the nations, but God said He would not go along (Exodus 33:3). Moses took one look at that deal and said, "If Your Presence does not go with us, do not lead us up from here" (Exodus 33:15). A great land without God in it is a bakery with no oven. Nice counters, nothing getting baked.

Notice how Moses got there, though. He had a tent outside the camp where the LORD spoke to him "face to face, as a man speaks to his friend" (Exodus 33:11). So when trouble came, Moses already knew where to go and Who to ask. He asked to know God's ways, and the LORD answered, "My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest" (Exodus 33:13-14). I think friendship with God gets built in the ordinary days, so you can lean on it when the hard one shows up.

Then Moses asks for even more: "Please show me Your glory" (Exodus 33:18). God does not say no to the asking. He says He will cause all His goodness to pass by, and He will have mercy on whom He has mercy (Exodus 33:19). He also says that no one can see His face and live, so He covers Moses with His hand and shows him His back (Exodus 33:20-23). Friend, you can ask God for BIG things, and even His protection is part of His goodness.
